title: Design: the Sales Type filter on Sales By Representative looks as designed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have two active staff members at the test location with their "Sales Representative" switch on, so that a work order can have a different Labor and Parts representative.
  • Use a customer with no Sales Representative assigned.
  • Have, today, one invoiced split work order for that customer (Labor set to one of them, Parts set to the other), one invoiced work order with one of them on both sides and one invoiced part sale with no shop supplies.
  • Set the browser window to 1440 pixels wide with the zoom at 100%.
  • Open the design pictures "sbr-06-a4-filter-open.png" (board 4.6) and "sbr-07-a4-sbr-labor-only.png" (board 4.7) attached to this case beside the browser window at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Open Reports > Sales By Representative for today in that browser window, with the Sales Type column turned on (as in the picture of board 4.7).
custom_steps:
1. Open the Sales Type filter and compare with the picture of board 4.6.
  2. Select only Labor and compare with the picture of board 4.7.
  3. Select all three again.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The filter lists "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales", all ticked.

Step 2:

  • Only the labor side of each work order shows, as in the picture.

Step 3:

  • All three are ticked again.
  • The filter reads "Sales Type: All".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative), story SV-11272 (Story 8, Filter both sales reports by Sales Type)

  • S8-R1: “Sales By Representative has a "Sales Type" filter with three options, in this order: "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales". All three are selected by default.”
  • S8-R3: “With all three selected the filter reads "Sales Type: All". With none it reads "Sales Type: None". Otherwise it reads the selected names in option order, for example "Sales Type: Labor, Parts".”
  • S5-R12: “With the Sales Type filter narrowed to Labor or to Parts, only that side's row shows (Story 8).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, boards 4.6 The Sales Type filter; 4.7 Labor only (the attached pictures are these boards).

Design pictures attached to this case: sbr-06-a4-filter-open.png, sbr-07-a4-sbr-labor-only.png.

  • Design — board 4.6 title: “4.6 The Sales Type filter”
  • Design — board 4.6 note: “Labor, Parts and Part Sales, all on by default. Rows and every total follow it; any combination works.”
  • Design — board 4.7 title: “4.7 Labor only”
  • Design — board 4.7 note: “"Sales Type: Labor" keeps only the labor side of each work order. (The Sales Type column is switched on in this board, from board 4.9.)”
